evidence.description: The response metadata is discarded and the body is decoded and processed unconditionally.

candidates.explanation: The network response is discarded, so HTTP status codes are never checked. A non-success response with a decodable body can update statistics, while other HTTP failures surface only as decoding errors rather than HTTP failures.
candidates.title: HTTP response status is ignored

evidence.description: A globally shared instance holds publicly readable mutable statistics.
The asynchronous method has no visible isolation and writes the statistic and its timestamp separately.
Another value and timestamp pair is also updated through separate assignments.

candidates.explanation: The shared Statistics instance exposes mutable state and an asynchronous update method without actor isolation or synchronization. Concurrent calls or reads can race with these mutations, and related values and timestamps are written separately rather than as one consistent update.
candidates.title: Shared mutable statistics lack concurrency protection

evidence.description: Numeric and date conversions represent failures as nil.
Trees are left unchanged if either conversion fails, and other numeric statistics silently fall back to their existing values.
Total investments are also silently left unchanged when the value or timestamp cannot be parsed.

candidates.explanation: Although fetchAndUpdate is throwing, failures to convert recognized statistics into numbers or dates are silently ignored. The method can return successfully after retaining old or hard-coded values for some statistics and updating others, without exposing that the refresh was incomplete.
candidates.title: Invalid statistic values silently produce incomplete updates
